25715.description: A launcher intended for use on cruiser-class spacecraft. While assault launchers do not possess the sheer damage-dealing capability of regular heavy missile launchers, their blend of speed and attack power lends them application across a good range of tactical situations.
25715.name: Heavy Assault Missile Launcher II

27413.description: A kinetic warhead designed for use with heavy assault launchers. Heavy assault missiles can be fired at a greater rate than heavy missiles, at the expense of effective range.
27413.name: Caldari Navy Scourge Heavy Assault Missile

28668.description:
A thick, heavy liquid, typically stored in tanks or container systems intended for liquids. It is composed of billions of nanites that can be programmed to repair damaged ship modules on the fly. The paste is simply applied to the damaged area, and the nanites meld into an exact copy of the damaged area, thus effecting repairs upon the module. This is a one-time process, as the nanites use themselves up along with the trace elements mixed into their carrier fluid.

The Repair Paste is generally only used for emergency on-site repairs. It is then recommended to have the damaged components looked at by a certified technician at first opportunity.
28668.name: Nanite Repair Paste

28756.description: Launcher for Core Scanner Probes and Combat Scanner Probes. Core Scanner Probes are used to scan down Cosmic Signatures in space. Combat Scanner Probes are used to scan down Cosmic Signatures, starships, structures and drones. Note: Only one scan probe launcher can be fitted per ship. 10% bonus to strength of scan probes.
28756.name: Sisters Expanded Probe Launcher

29990.description: For many Minmatar, the high mountains of Matar hold wonders unknown to the rest of New Eden: hidden glens, beautiful creatures, buried customs. Not surprisingly, the Krusual tribe lay claim to these mountains, their home for generations and base to their machinations. Krusual elders whisper ancient tales among their huddled tribes, describing the glory of heroes past and enigmatic prophecies of old. On the darkest day, at the most hopeless moments, an elder may speak of Loki, in reverent tones and excited hushes. In the ancient tongue, the Loki are the crux of Krusual thought. There is no direct translation for this word; in fact, Loki translates differently among the elders. It can mean “hidden wonder” or “secret passage”, “changing mask” or “unseen dagger”. Regardless of its context, Loki has one meaning common to all its tales across all the elders: “hope”.
29990.name: Loki

30486.description: A scanner probe used for scanning down Cosmic Signatures, starships, structures and drones. Can be launched from Expanded Probe Launchers.
30486.name: Sisters Combat Scanner Probe

31754.description: This ship modification is designed to increase the thermal resistance of ship shields at the expense of increased signature radius. Penalty: Using more than one type of this module or similar modules that affect the same attribute on the ship will be penalized. The drawbacks of fitting this rig may be reduced by training the Shield Rigging skill.
31754.name: Medium Thermal Shield Reinforcer I

31796.description: This ship modification is designed to increase shield capacity at the expense of increased signature radius. The drawbacks of fitting this rig may be reduced by training the Shield Rigging skill.
31796.name: Medium Core Defense Field Extender II

31932.description: Increases the maximum strength of the shield.
31932.name: Republic Fleet Large Shield Extender

35659.description:
Massive boost to speed for a very short time. The thrust that boosts the ship, and the corresponding maximum velocity bonus, are limited by the mass of the ship that uses this module. The sheer amount of energy needed to power this system means that it must permanently reserve a fraction of the capacitor output just to maintain the integrity of its warp containment field, and when activated it substantially increases the ship's EM footprint.

Penalty: Max capacitor reduced.

Note: Usually fit on Cruisers and Battlecruisers.
35659.name: 50MN Y-T8 Compact Microwarpdrive

45595.description:
From the moment Strategic Cruisers became a reality, there were whispers amongst the scientific community about the potential for advances in cloaking technology. They remained that alone for the longest time, with few involved in the reverse engineering process willing to share any news of their discoveries. Everyone knew that, should the technology ever become a reality, the capabilities of the new Strategic Cruisers would change overnight.    

The Loki's Covert Reconfiguration designs arose out of a collective will to respond to what was thought to be Amarrian aggression deep inside their home regions. Unlike many scientific and technological breakthroughs, it was not the Sebiestor tribe alone who ushered in the paradigm shift to covert-capable Strategic Cruisers. It was only through consultation and collaboration with many other tribes and sub-factions that something substantial began to take shape. 

The Krusual and Thukker are said to have played the most important roles, however, in realizing the final design; the Thukker by providing the cloaking technology, and the Krusual by convincing them to do so. How they achieved this, or what they may have promised remains a secret; the two tribes are notorious for having many, and keeping them all.
45595.name: Loki Defensive - Covert Reconfiguration

45608.description: Adaptation and innovation go hand-in-hand, and this subsystem is a prime example of both ideas. While researching Sleeper drone weapon systems, a group of Minmatar engineers discovered that Sleeper launcher hardpoint design allowed for a vast increase to the rate of fire without increasing powergrid requirements. The resulting subsystem allows the Loki to achieve some of the most aggressive missile configurations seen on any cruiser.
45608.name: Loki Offensive - Launcher Efficiency Configuration

45620.description: Constructed from hard yet lightweight fullerene polymers, these intercalated fibers boost the speed and agility of a starship without compromising its structural resilience. Even though basic nanofibers have existed for hundreds of years, the integration of various Sleeper-based salvage and other polymers takes the technology to a completely new level of modularity. This has allowed the same centuries-old technology to be ported over to the new Tech III paradigm.
45620.name: Loki Propulsion - Intercalated Nanofibers

45633.description: Even millennia old, the technology employed by Sleeper drones is far from lacking. This is particularly true in the field of interdiction technology, where their capabilities often exceed contemporary systems. Consequently, this aspect of their fearsome arsenal has been the focus of much study and in some rare cases, the starting point for scientific breakthroughs. Minmatar researchers studied the long-range webification systems of the Sleeper drones from the moment they were discovered, quickly reverse engineering a subsystem for their Loki that could replicate the Sleeper's own offensive modules. The end result is a noticeable amplification of a stasis webifier's effective range.
45633.name: Loki Core - Immobility Drivers

45998.description: +3% turret damage, +3% missile damage, 3% vorton projector damage. Duration 30 minutes. A novel and powerful addition to the range of neural boosters available to capsuleers, the Agency's ‘Pyrolancea’ compounds introduce a temporary but highly adaptive neural lace into the user’s synaptic structures. This 'Pyrolancea' lace enhances neural centers involved in calibration of munitions payloads and weapons energy profiles on the fly during high-intensity combat. The increase in the processing available to the capsuleer means that payload calibration solutions can be tailored more finely and results in improved damage yields against any given target. Compounds with the Agency identifier are being seeded into target locations identified by the mysterious network ahead of sponsored operations. Entities occupying the target sites often collect the Agency's support drops themselves even if they realize what they must portend. The Agency’s novel method of supporting capsuleer operations is thought to be as much an experiment as it is an incentive for freelance pilots to take up the public contracts.
45998.name: Agency 'Pyrolancea' DB3 Dose I

45999.description: +5% turret damage, +5% missile damage, 5% vorton projector damage. Duration 30 minutes. A novel and powerful addition to the range of neural boosters available to capsuleers, the Agency's ‘Pyrolancea’ compounds introduce a temporary but highly adaptive neural lace into the user’s synaptic structures. This 'Pyrolancea' lace enhances neural centers involved in calibration of munitions payloads and weapons energy profiles on the fly during high-intensity combat. The increase in the processing available to the capsuleer means that payload calibration solutions can be tailored more finely and results in improved damage yields against any given target. Compounds with the Agency identifier are being seeded into target locations identified by the mysterious network ahead of sponsored operations. Entities occupying the target sites often collect the Agency's support drops themselves even if they realize what they must portend. The Agency’s novel method of supporting capsuleer operations is thought to be as much an experiment as it is an incentive for freelance pilots to take up the public contracts.
45999.name: Agency 'Pyrolancea' DB5 Dose II

expected.note: Real pyfa cross-check (2026-10-10) against killmail 138935092 -- a Loki (T3 Strategic Cruiser), 5x Heavy Assault Missile Launcher II/Mjolnir Rage Heavy Assault Missile, 3x Ballistic Control System II, Republic Fleet Large Shield Extender + 50MN Y-T8 Compact MWD + 2x Stasis Webifier II + Warp Disruptor II, Damage Control II, 2x Medium Core Defense Field Extender II + Medium Thermal Shield Reinforcer I rigs, standard Loki subsystems (Immobility Drivers/Covert Reconfiguration/Launcher Efficiency Configuration/Intercalated Nanofibers). pyfa reported DPS 801 (exact match to the tool own dpsFixed) and EHP 33.9k/shield 21.4k/armor 6.29k/hull 6.22k -- all consistent with the tool own computed exact values (33896/21386/6291/6219), which round to those same pyfa figures. unmatchedWeaponCount=1 is the Sisters Expanded Probe Launcher, a known cosmetic-only miscount (KNOWN OPEN ITEM #2 in [[dscan-tool]] -- Probe Launchers misclassified as unresolved weapons, no false DPS). Scaffolded via scaffold_golden_fit.mjs (Phase 5) from a real, live-fetched killmail (not hand-typed) -- the first golden fit built this way, and the first closed-loop proof the scaffolder pipeline end-to-end (live fetch -> assembly -> provisional compute -> real pyfa confirmation) actually works. Loki sensor-strength re-investigation ADDED 2026-10-11: sensorStrengthValue now asserts this fit genuinely has NO sensor-strength bonus -- the previously-flagged open gap (pyfa figure 20.4 vs. this tool 17, Ladar) is RESOLVED as a different-subsystem mismatch, not a bug. Confirmed live via ESI across all 3 real variants of each of the Loki Core/Defensive/Offensive/Propulsion Subsystem slots (12 types total) that only one -- Loki Core - Dissolution Sequencer (type 45631), NOT Immobility Drivers (type 45633, what THIS killmail actually fitted) -- carries any effect touching sensor-strength attributes 208-211 (a PostPercent bonus to Ladar/209 via container attribute 1446, itself scaled by Minmatar Core Systems skill -- same required-skill-scales-a-container-attribute architecture as the earlier Tengu/Proteus EWAR bug). 17 base x 1.20 (Dissolution Sequencer @ Minmatar Core Systems V, by this codebase established per-level pattern) = 20.4, an exact match to the pasted pyfa figure -- strong evidence pyfa was showing a Loki fitted WITH Dissolution Sequencer, not this fit's actual Immobility Drivers. See dscan-tool-architecture.md and the SCAN_STRENGTH_ATTRS comment in dscan-tool.html. UPDATE (independent review finding #18, 2026-10-11): KNOWN OPEN ITEM #2 (Probe Launcher miscounted as an unresolved weapon) is now FIXED -- weaponCategoryFromGroup() returning null for the Sisters Expanded Probe Launcher (Scan Probe Launcher group) is now checked BEFORE incrementing variableWeaponCount/pushing to unresolvedWeapons, not after, so it is excluded from this accounting entirely instead of permanently stuck as unresolved. variableWeaponCount 6->5 (the probe launcher no longer counted at all), unmatchedWeaponCount 1->0 (nothing left unresolved -- all 5 real HAM II launchers are confirmed via their loaded Mjolnir Rage charge, as before). UPDATE 2026-10-11 (backlog #1): speedCruising/alignTimeBase added -- this real killmail fit already has 45620 (Loki Propulsion - Intercalated Nanofibers) fitted, confirmed live via ESI to carry the exact same +5%/lvl maxVelocity / -5%/lvl agility magnitude as Legion's 45611 (Minmatar Propulsion Systems skill@V scaling 1450/1523 the same way Amarr's scales 1435/1512 for Legion -- see SUBSYSTEM_SPEED_AGILITY_BONUS's comment). Hand-derived: 185*1.25*1.25=289.06 (289); -ln(0.25)*(0.54*0.75*0.75)*13.8=5.81 (5.8) -- exact tool match, confirms the table applies correctly for a 2nd race via a real (not constructed) fit. UPDATE 2026-10-11 (backlog #16, NEGATIVE CONTROL): capacitorCapacity (1875) pinned -- this fit's Core subsystem (if any) is not one of the capacitor-bonus 'Reactor' ids, confirming SUBSYSTEM_CAPACITOR_CAPACITY_SELFADD_ATTR correctly contributes zero here. CORRECTED 2026-10-12: the 2026-10-11 re-investigation above reached the right final number (20.4) via the WRONG mechanism (misattributed to a different Loki Core subsystem, Dissolution Sequencer, that this kill never fitted) -- the real root cause, found via Erik real Svipul-fit bug report (KNOWN OPEN ITEM #1 in dscan-tool.md), is the universal Ladar Sensor Compensation skill (type 33001, ESI skill group 1213 "Targeting" -- the very group the original check claimed to have exhaustively ruled out), +20% at V, independent of subsystem entirely. Tool fixed to apply MAX_SENSOR_COMPENSATION_MULT=1.20 to every ship sensor-strength figure; this fit sensorStrengthValue expectation updated 17->20.4 to match the corrected formula (and the pyfa figure that was on file the whole time). See dscan-tool.html SCAN_STRENGTH_ATTRS comment for the full corrected mechanism writeup.

UPDATE 2026-10-11 (independent review pass, finding #1): this fit's Small Auxiliary Nano Pump II is a Rig Armor (confirmed live, group 773), which carries attribute 1138 as an AGILITY drawback (own description: "at the expense of agility"), not a signature-radius one -- the old code wrongly pooled every rig's 1138 into sig radius unconditionally; fixed to gate sig-radius pooling to Rig Shield only and add a parallel agility-drawback pool for Rig Armor. Not independently pyfa-cross-checked (same bar as the rest of this fit), but the mechanism itself (effect 2717 modifying attribute 70 via 1138) was confirmed live via raw ESI dogma effect bodies, not assumed. UPDATE 2026-10-11 (backlog #10): added signatureRadiusBase/Boosted (39/234) as a non-Interceptor control for the new Interceptor MWD-sig-bloom-reduction fix -- Ishkur is an Assault Frigate (group 324), not group 831, so this fit's own MWD gets no reduction; confirms the fix doesn't touch it. This type's cached dogma_attributes stub was missing attribute 90 entirely (predating this feature) -- added with the live-confirmed value rather than guessed. Chosen as the Nosferatu golden-fit coverage specifically because it is a REAL fitted module on a real killmail-derived fit already in this file, not a synthetic addition. Also discovered while verifying the Nosferatu assertions above: this hull stub was missing dogma attribute 55 (capacitorRechargeTime) entirely, predating the 2026-10-12 capacitor-stability feature -- without it rechargeTimeSec computed as 0, which the stability guard (capacity<=0||rechargeTimeSec<=0) degrades to a meaningless stable:true/stablePct:null ("Stable at null%" on screen, caught via this fix's own Playwright verification screenshot). Added the live-confirmed value (187500ms, ref-data.everef.net/types/12042) and now pins capacitorStable=1/capacitorStablePct=56.8/capacitorWeak=0 as a second real-fit capacitor-stability regression guard alongside the Curse/Rifter ones (this one exercising the stable-but-not-super-healthy middle case, with a genuine small active cap-warfare drain from its own fitted Nosferatu/Scrambler). UPDATE 2026-10-12 (reverted): the hasCapLeanAlert=0 assertion above has been REMOVED -- that whole alert was pulled from the EWAR card per Erik (redundant with the existing capacitorWeak=0 signal already pinned above, which stays). UPDATE 2026-10-12 (Capacitor Booster gain modeling): verifying this feature against every existing golden fit surfaced that this fit ALSO carries a real fitted Capacitor Booster (Small Capacitor Booster II, type 3568) -- not previously noticed, since earlier capacitor-feature work on this fit focused on its Nosferatu/Scrambler. It has no loaded Cap Booster charge in this fit's data (a synthetic/constructed fit built for dual-prop-mod/sig-radius testing, not charge-loadout fidelity), so this is the honest 'module fitted, charge unidentified' disclosure path -- pins capacitorHasCapBooster=1/capacitorChargeUnidentified=1 (no capacitorBoosted* fields, same convention as a fit with no 2nd prop mod having no speedSecondaryBoosted), confirming the card discloses this honestly rather than silently showing nothing or guessing. UPDATE 2026-10-12 (bounded-range follow-up): verifying the new no-identified-charge range fallback against this fit's own real fitted Small Capacitor Booster II (type 3568, no loaded charge anywhere in this fit's data) surfaced ANOTHER pre-existing fixture gap -- this type's cached dogma_attributes stub was missing attribute 73 (REP_CYCLE_DURATION_ATTR) entirely, so the range calculation silently produced nothing (same failure shape as the earlier attr-90/attr-55 gaps found this same session). Added the live-confirmed value (12000ms, ref-data.everef.net/types/3568) -- now pins capacitorRangeMinGainPerSec=2.1/capacitorRangeMaxGainPerSec=33.3/capacitorRangeMinStable=1/capacitorRangeMaxStable=1/capacitorRangeMinStablePct=72.1/capacitorRangeMaxStablePct=100. Hand-verified: this module's own 15 m3 charge-bay capacity (attribute 38) excludes every charge tier above Navy Cap Booster 400 (12 m3, 400 GJ) -- the plain Cap Booster 400 (16 m3) does NOT fit, confirming the volume-bound (not a hardcoded tier cutoff) is doing real work here: min=25 GJ/12s=2.08~2.1 GJ/s (smallest charge that exists, always fits any real module), max=400 GJ/12s=33.3 GJ/s (Navy Cap Booster 400, the largest charge that actually fits this specific module's hold).

expected.note: EWAR capabilities card regression guard (F3, 2026-10-11), built from a real, live-ESI-fetched loss (zKillboard 139073592, hash dc40ad4503d86ee8f768695ef2078ccdd9561f0d) chosen specifically because it stacks 3 distinct EWAR module types across both tracked categories on one hull: Caldari Navy Warp Disruptor (tackle/scram, 26km, strength 1), Guidance Disruptor II (disrupt, 48km, missileVelocityBonusPct=-9/flightTimeBonusPct=-9), and 2x Tracking Disruptor II (disrupt, 48km each, opticalBonusPct=-17.19/falloffBonusPct=-17.19/trackingSpeedBonusPct=-17.19) -- 4 modules total, 3 distinct names, confirming both the shared-ESI-group-291 name-based split (Tracking vs. Guidance Disruptor) and the longest-range-first sort (both 48km disruptors ahead of the 26km scram). This fit also happens to carry zero turrets/launchers (all 5 high slots are cap warfare: 3x Small + 2x Medium Energy Neutralizer II), so dpsFixed/droneDps/HP below come entirely from the drone bay (5x Acolyte II + 3x Infiltrator II, Hornet EC-300 ECM drones excluded as non-combat) and the fitted Medium Ancillary Armor Repairer (296x Nanite Repair Paste charges) -- these are the tool's own sandbox-computed values (not independently pyfa-cross-checked, since this fit's purpose is EWAR coverage, not DPS methodology) and are pinned at a wide tolerance purely as a 'did anything else regress' guard, not a precision claim. UPDATED 2026-10-11 (EWAR effectiveness bonuses, F-item): ewarLongestRangeM/ewarTdRangeM/ewarGdRangeM now 72000 (was 48000) -- Long Distance Jamming (+50%@V, universal skill) boosts Tracking/Guidance Disruptor optimal range, 48000*1.5=72000. The 3 Tracking Disruptor magnitude fields (optical/falloff/tracking speed) and 4 Guidance Disruptor ones (missile velocity/flight time/explosion velocity/explosion radius) are boosted by TWO independent multiplicative sources confirmed live via ESI and pyfa cross-validation (2026-10-11): the Curse hull's own Amarr Cruiser skill bonus (+37.5%@V Weapon Disruption effectiveness, effect 6395) AND the universal Weapon Destabilization skill (+25%@V to the same 7 attributes, effects 3561/5793/6386, type 19767) -- these stack multiplicatively (1.375 x 1.25 = 1.71875), not just the hull bonus alone (an earlier version of this fit asserted hull-only values of -23.63625/-12.375/-16.5/+16.5, which pyfa's real numbers -29.5%/-20.6% proved incomplete -- Weapon Destabilization was the missing piece). base -17.19 * 1.71875 = -29.5453125 (tracking disruptor), base -9/-9/-12/+12 * 1.71875 = -15.46875/-15.46875/-20.625/+20.625 (guidance disruptor). ewarScramRangeM pinned at 26000 (unchanged) as a negative-path guard -- no skill or hull bonus found anywhere that touches Warp Scrambler/Disruptor strength OR a Curse's own (nonexistent) scram range bonus. UPDATE 2026-10-11 (comprehensive skill audit, P1-B): drone DPS multiplier corrected -- the RoF reduction previously applied (-20%, attributed to '[Race] Drone Specialization') was fictional, no drone RoF skill exists at all; that skill is actually a +10%@V DAMAGE bonus gated to T2 drones (reqSkill-detected), and a separate, previously entirely unmodeled weapon-size-class damage skill (+25%@V, Light/Medium/Heavy Drone Operation or Sentry Drone Interfacing, always applies) was added. Net real multiplier for a T1 drone is unchanged (1.50x1.25=1.875, same magnitude as the old 1.50/0.80 by coincidence); for a T2 drone it's 1.50x1.25x1.10=2.0625, ~10% higher than before. Separately, this fit's cached Acolyte II/Infiltrator II type snapshots were stale (missing reqSkill attributes 182/183/184 entirely, predating this file's need to read them) -- refreshed with full live ESI data 2026-10-11 as part of this same fix, which is why droneDps moved further than the formula alone would predict (138 -> 229, not just a ~10% bump) for this specific fit only. UPDATE 2026-10-11 (independent review pass, finding #2): maxActiveDrones (attribute 352) was discovered to be a CHARACTER attribute, not a ship one -- confirmed live via ESI's own attribute metadata and the absence of 352 from every checked ship's dogma_attributes -- so the old Infinity fallback was never actually a fallback at all; it was the value used on EVERY fit, unconditionally. Fixed to the correct fixed cap of 5 (MAX_ACTIVE_DRONES_SKILL_V, from the Drones skill's own description: 'Can operate 1 drone per skill level', assumed trained to V per this tool's established convention). This fit's drone bay held more than 5 combat-capable drones, so it was previously crediting more active drones than a pilot can actually control -- the corrected sandbox output (droneCount now exactly 5, greedily filled hardest-hitting-type-first, same already-audited per-drone formula) is the new expected value. Sandbox: droneCount=5 of 8 bay (3x Infiltrator II + 2x Acolyte II deployed, hardest-hitting-first), dpsFixed=droneDps=177 (unchanged: this fit has no turrets/launchers fitted, all 5 high slots are cap warfare). Every EWAR field (ewar*) is untouched by this fix -- confirmed identical to the pre-fix values above. UPDATE 2026-10-12 (export-fit-to-clipboard backlog item): also now pins expected.eftExportText -- the exact fitToEftText() serialization of this fit (chosen for this assertion specifically because it exercises every rack: Low/Mid/High slots, Rigs, Drone bay, Cargo -- the richest real-killmail fit already in this file), format confirmed against pyfa's own real exporter (service/port/eft.py). Catches any future regression in the serializer itself or in the module/charge pairing it shares with classifyHighSlotItem(). UPDATE 2026-10-12 (capacitor stability backlog #2): also pins capacitorStable=0/capacitorTimeToEmptySec=21.3/capacitorWeak=1 -- this fit (5 cap warfare high slots: 2x Medium + 3x Small Energy Neutralizer II, all with their own capacitorNeed) is genuinely cap-unstable under this tool's sustained-everything-cycling model, verified via simulateCapacitorStability() (see dscan-tool.html comment block) sandbox output, not independently pyfa-cross-checked for this exact number (same evidentiary bar as this fit's other non-pyfa-verified fields, see note above) -- picked as the unstable-case regression guard specifically because it is a REAL killmail fit already in this file, not synthetic. UPDATE 2026-10-12 (cap warfare backlog, Erik overnight request: tie energy neuts/nosferatu into the EWAR card): ewarModuleCount 4->9 and ewarTypeCount 3->5 -- this fit's 2x Medium + 3x Small Energy Neutralizer II (5 modules, 2 distinct type names) now correctly count as EWAR (new drain category, own badge color/letter C) alongside the pre-existing 3 disrupt-category items, a deliberate behavior change from adding Energy Neutralizer/Energy Nosferatu (group ids 71/68, confirmed live via ref-data.everef.net) to EWAR_GROUP_INFO, not a regression. UPDATE 2026-10-12 (cap warfare backlog continued): also pins ewarNeutRangeM/ewarNeutFalloffM/ewarNeutCapPerCycle/ewarNeutCapPerSec (5000m/2500m/55 GJ per 6s cycle/9.17 GJ/s) for the first-matching neut module (Small Energy Neutralizer II, byKind picks first array match) -- confirmed live via ref-data.everef.net/types/13003 (energyNeutralizerAmount=55, duration=6000ms). UPDATE 2026-10-12 (cap-lean neut-vulnerability alert, Erik overnight request, EWAR/Misc card): also pins hasCapLeanAlert=1 -- this fit is already cap-unstable on its own (capacitorStable=0 above), so the new opportunity-severity misc trait ("Cap-lean target", blue badge, distinct from the red danger badge) correctly fires, reusing the exact same capWeak signal as the Weaknesses card's existing flag, just offense-framed on the EWAR card per Erik's request. UPDATE 2026-10-12 (reverted): the hasCapLeanAlert assertion above/the EWAR-card alert it pinned has been REMOVED per Erik -- he caught that it was the exact same capWeak/stablePct/netRate signal as this fit's own capacitorStable/capacitorTimeToEmptySec/capacitorWeak assertions already pinned above, just restated in a second place. The Weaknesses-card capWeakReason wording was lightly reworded instead (now also states the GJ/s margin number) rather than removed, since that's the one place this signal belongs. UPDATE 2026-10-12 (Capacitor Booster gain modeling, Erik-approved follow-up: "are we accounting for cap boosters... yes please", then "in the capacitor section, let's have an indicator next to the stability indicator showing that it's boosted. maybe show both boosted and unboosted values?"): this fit's real fitted Medium F-RX Compact Capacitor Booster (type 4833) + loaded Navy Cap Booster 800 charge (type 32014), sharing Mid-slot flag 19 -- confirmed via this fit's own real killmail item data, zero new fixture data needed -- now pins capacitorHasCapBooster=1/capacitorChargeUnidentified=0/capacitorBoostedGainPerSec=62.7/capacitorBoostedStable=0/capacitorBoostedTimeToEmptySec=80.3. Grounded live via ref-data.everef.net: attribute 67 (capacitorBonus) on the charge = 800 GJ total deliverable, attribute 73 (cycle duration) on the module = 12750ms -> this fit's gain figure (62.7 GJ/s) is the module's own fitted quantity (1) x 800/12.75s; since this fit is already cap-unstable even unboosted (capacitorStable=0 above), the boosted figure is ALSO unstable (capacitorBoostedStable=0) but survives far longer before running dry (80.3s vs. 21.3s unboosted) -- exercises the 'boosted but still not actually stable' branch of simulateCapacitorStability(), the one case the other 2 golden fits below don't cover. UPDATE 2026-10-12 (Capacitor Booster cargo-inference + bounded-range follow-up, Erik: "add the cargo-inference fallback and use a bounded range for the no-data case"): also pins capacitorBoostedFromCargo=0 -- this real fit's Capacitor Booster charge is genuinely FLAG-paired (not inferred from cargo), confirming the new cargo-inference code path doesn't fire when a real loaded charge is already identified. See the new curse_constructed_cap_booster_cargo_inference golden fit (a deliberately modified clone of this same real killmail, with the flag-19 charge item removed) for the cargo-inference-DOES-fire case. UPDATE 2026-10-12 (turret "No answer" fallback-to-2nd-weakest backlog item, Erik: "extend weakness info for weapon systems with 'No answer' to utilize the next weakest resist type to pick an ammo type ... flagging that it cannot take advantage of the primary weakness"): also pins turretLaserName='Radio'/turretLaserFallback=1 -- this fit's weakest damage type is Thermal (laser can never address Thermal at all, see TURRET_RECS), so laser now falls back to this fit's SECOND-weakest type (EM, laser's one true answer) instead of a dead-end 'No answer' -- the fallback-succeeds case. turretHybridName='Iridium or Thorium'/turretHybridFallback=0 and turretProjectileName='Phased Plasma'/turretProjectileFallback=0 pin the unchanged direct-hit behavior for the other two systems (both already answer Thermal directly, no fallback needed), confirming the new buildTurretRecs() logic is a no-op for systems that didn't need it.

expected.note: CONSTRUCTED, disclosed -- see label. Isolates the Controlled Bursts (3316, -25%@V turret capacitorNeed) fix: capacitorActiveDrainPerSec = round((36*0.75) / effectiveCycleSec, 1dp). UPDATED 2026-10-11 (independent review backlog #15, cap-drain RoF-consistency fix): effectiveCycleSec now correctly includes the turret RoF skill assumption (MAX_TURRET_ROF_MULT=0.80*0.90=0.72, same multiplier the DPS calc itself applies to this exact attribute) on top of the raw 7875ms rateOfFire -- round(27 / (7.875*0.72), 1dp) = round(27/5.67, 1dp) = round(4.7619, 1dp) = 4.8. Was locked in at 3.4 (round(27/7.875,1dp)) before this fix, which used the RAW un-boosted cycle time -- a real self-consistency bug (cap drain and DPS read the same RATE_OF_FIRE_ATTR but only DPS applied the RoF skill multiplier to it), not a live-ESI question. Rifter carries no energy-weapon-category SHIP_ROLE_BONUS rof entry, so catMod.rofMult=1 here and the only multiplier in play is the universal max-skill assumption. Verified directly against the tool's own sandboxed estimateHpAndDps() output post-fix: 4.8 exact.

expected.note: CONSTRUCTED, disclosed -- see label. Isolates the T1-vs-T2 missile-launcher RoF gating fix: this T1 launcher requires only Missile Launcher Operation (3319), NOT Heavy Missile Specialization (20211), so MISSILE_SPECIALIZATION_ROF_MULT must NOT apply. Hand-derived: perShot = 149(kin) * 1(no launcher damageMultiplier) * (1.10 WarheadUpgrades x 1.25 HeavyMissiles-sizeclass = 1.375 dmgSkillMult) = 204.875. rofSkillMult = 0.85(RapidLaunch) x 0.90(MissileLauncherOperation) = 0.765 (missileSpecMult=1, not gated). effectiveCycleSec = 15 * 0.765 = 11.475s. dpsFixed = 204.875/11.475 = 17.86 (was 19.84 pre-fix, when the T2-only Specialization 0.90 factor was wrongly applied universally -- exactly the predicted 1/0.9=1.111x overstatement). Live-verified via ESI 2026-10-11 (type 501 Heavy Missile Launcher I, type 209 Scourge Heavy Missile).

rifter_constructed_rig_drawback_routing.label: CONSTRUCTED (disclosed, see expected.note): bare Rifter + 1x Small Trimark Armor Pump I (armor rig) + 1x Small Core Defense Field Extender I (shield rig) in rig slots, nothing else fitted -- isolates the rig-drawback routing fix (independent review finding #1, 2026-10-11) using real live-ESI-verified attributes: both rigs carry the exact same raw attribute 1138 value (10), but confirmed live via each rig's own effect modifier body that Rig Armor (773) routes 1138 to ship attribute 70 (agility) via effect 2717, while Rig Shield (774) routes it to ship attribute 552 (signature radius) via effect 2716 -- two genuinely different target stats sharing one raw-magnitude attribute. Before this fix, BOTH rigs' 1138 were pooled into signature radius unconditionally (no group check), inflating sig radius by the armor rig's unrelated agility-drawback number while never touching agility at all.

10631.description: A tiny launcher that can carry a very limited supply of rockets. Not really intended as a primary weapon but rather as a cheap supplementary weapon system.

expected.note: CONSTRUCTED, disclosed -- see label. Hand-derived: droneSkillDmgMult = 1.5(DroneInterfacing V) * 1.25(Sentry Drone Interfacing size-class, reqSkill182=23594) * 1.10(Gallente Drone Specialization racial, reqSkill183=12486) = 2.0625. dmgPerCycle = 64(thermal) * 1.65(own mult) * 2.0625(skillMult) * 1.5(Dominix hull dronesentry-fallback-to-drone dmg bonus, post-fix) = 326.7; perDroneDps = 326.7/4s = 81.675. Bandwidth check: Dominix droneBandwidth=125 / Garde II bandwidthUsed=25 = floor 5, which equals the MAX_ACTIVE_DRONES_SKILL_V=5 character cap (finding #2) -- both bind at exactly 5, so all 5 bay drones are active. droneDps = 5 * 81.675 = 408.375 -> see actual sandbox output for exact rounding. Pre-fix (dronesentry categoryMods.dmgMult=1.0 instead of 1.5) this would show droneDps = 5*54.45 = 272.25 -> ~272, a 1.5x ratio that exactly matches the predicted magnitude of the fix. Live-verified via ESI 2026-10-11 (type 645 Dominix, type 28211 Garde II).

This is a materially worse overstatement than the turret-size case (2x) and was the more urgent half of this backlog item. ammoEstimates dps for Mjolnir Rocket sandbox-verified exact at 12. Pre-fix (old code, no Interceptor-group check), boosted would have been 210 -- identical to what a non-Interceptor hull with the exact same MWD shows (confirmed: a Rifter fit with this same 5MN Y-T8 MWD also gives boosted=210) -- a ~2.7x overstatement of how much an Interceptor's signature actually blooms under MWD. Mechanism: Crow's own live dogma carries attribute 568 (eliteBonusInterceptor) = -15 (confirmed, same on all 10 group-831 hulls) and effect 3766 (interceptorMWDSignatureRadiusBonus, modifies attribute 554 by 568's value) -- at assumed Interceptors@V (-15 x 5 = -75%), the MWD's own 500% sig bonus becomes 500 x 0.25 = 125%, giving boosted = 35 x 2.25 = 78.75 (rounds to 79). See INTERCEPTOR_GROUP_ID/INTERCEPTOR_MWD_SIG_BONUS_ATTR comment block in dscan-tool.html for the full live-ESI grounding (effect 3766's modifiers, cross-checked against EVE University's Crow page and pyfa's own eos/effects.py Effect6730 for where in the math this reduction has to apply).

expected.note: Live-ESI-grounded 2026-10-11 (backlog #1): Proteus hull (29988: maxVelocity 230, agility 0.56, mass 13,300,000 -- all live-ESI) + Hyperspatial Optimization (45617) fitted, nothing else. Confirmed via ESI that Proteus's 'speed+agility' Propulsion subsystem variant is GENUINELY ASYMMETRIC vs. every other race: its own in-game description says 'improves the agility AND WARP SPEED' -- agility -7.5%/lvl (attr 1520, effect subsystemBonusGallentePropulsion2Agility) -> -37.5%@V (Gallente Propulsion Systems skill@V scaling, effects 3850/4213), but it does NOT touch maxVelocity at all (0, confirmed, not an oversight) -- instead a +10%/lvl warpSpeedMultiplier bonus (attr 1440, effect subsystemBonusGallentePropulsionWarpSpeed) -> +50%@V, which this tool doesn't model anywhere (no warp-speed figure exists in the Speed/Align card) and is disclosed as a deliberately out-of-scope gap, not silently dropped. This fit pins exactly that asymmetry: speedCruising UNCHANGED from the no-bonus baseline (230*1.25=287.5, rounds to 288) while alignTimeBase reflects the real -37.5%@V agility cut (-ln(0.25)*(0.56*0.75*0.625)*13.3=4.84, rounds to 4.8). If a future change ever mistakenly gives Proteus a maxVelocity bonus (e.g. by copying another race's table entry), this fit's speedCruising assertion catches it immediately. 29990.description: For many Minmatar, the high mountains of Matar hold wonders unknown to the rest of New Eden: hidden glens, beautiful creatures, buried customs. Not surprisingly, the Krusual tribe lay claim to these mountains, their home for generations and base to their machinations. Krusual elders whisper ancient tales among their huddled tribes, describing the glory of heroes past and enigmatic prophecies of old. On the darkest day, at the most hopeless moments, an elder may speak of Loki, in reverent tones and excited hushes. In the ancient tongue, the Loki are the crux of Krusual thought. There is no direct translation for this word; in fact, Loki translates differently among the elders. It can mean “hidden wonder” or “secret passage”, “changing mask” or “unseen dagger”. Regardless of its context, Loki has one meaning common to all its tales across all the elders: “hope”.
29990.name: Loki

47918.description:
This medium-sized Entropic Disintegrator is normally seen in use on Triglavian cruisers or battlecruisers, which are able to handle the increased radiation and serious gravitational tidal forces the weapon generates as a side-effect of its operation.

Entropic Disintegrators draw on the tremendous power of the Triglavian singularity-based energy systems to convert exotic matter into a particle stream directed with locally generated entropic force. While powerful, the range of the weapon is limited by the attenuation of entropic forces, which dissipate critically beyond the optimal range. As a result this weapon has no falloff range.

The particle stream generates thermal and explosive reactions on impact, and the entropic forces resolve into a localized gravitational conduit that steadily increases the acceleration on the exotic particles. In effect, the weapon's damage potential increases to a maximum level as long as the particle stream is kept on the same target.

Requires either standard or advanced exotic plasma charge ammo types: Baryon, Meson, Tetryon, Mystic, and Occult.
47918.name: Heavy Entropic Disintegrator II

47929.description:
An Entropic Disintegrator uses charges of exotic plasma to provide the particle feedstock for the weapon's beam, with different forms of exotic matter modulating the beam's characteristics.

Meson Exotic Plasma charges yield a beam with a very long range but reduced thermal and explosive damage potential.
47929.name: Meson Exotic Plasma M

expected.note: Confirmed via the real estimateHpAndDps() run against this live-ESI data 2026-10-11: signatureRadius={base:35, boosted:79}. Pre-fix (old code, no Interceptor-group check), boosted would have been 210 -- identical to what a non-Interceptor hull with the exact same MWD shows (confirmed: a Rifter fit with this same 5MN Y-T8 MWD also gives boosted=210) -- a ~2.7x overstatement of how much an Interceptor's signature actually blooms under MWD. Mechanism: Crow's own live dogma carries attribute 568 (eliteBonusInterceptor) = -15 (confirmed, same on all 10 group-831 hulls) and effect 3766 (interceptorMWDSignatureRadiusBonus, modifies attribute 554 by 568's value) -- at assumed Interceptors@V (-15 x 5 = -75%), the MWD's own 500% sig bonus becomes 500 x 0.25 = 125%, giving boosted = 35 x 2.25 = 78.75 (rounds to 79). See INTERCEPTOR_GROUP_ID/INTERCEPTOR_MWD_SIG_BONUS_ATTR comment block in dscan-tool.html for the full live-ESI grounding (effect 3766's modifiers, cross-checked against EVE University's Crow page and pyfa's own eos/effects.py Effect6730 for where in the math this reduction has to apply). MISSILE APPLICATION ASSERTIONS ADDED 2026-10-11 (missile damage-application-efficiency feature, missile-side only per user direction): cruising state (sig=35, speed=538 -- unboosted, MWD off) ranks Rocket best at 63.0%; boosted state (sig=79, speed=3790 -- MWD on, both numbers already independently verified by this fit's own pre-existing signatureRadiusBase/Boosted assertions) ranks Rocket best at 30.2% -- application drops sharply once the MWD both blooms the Crow's own signature AND multiplies its speed by ~7x, confirming the dual-state pairing never cross-mixes base-sig with boosted-speed or vice versa (which would produce very different, physically-nonsensical numbers). Hand-derived boosted Rocket fraction (sig=79, speed=3790 from this fit's own rounded display values) gives 30.3%, 0.1pp off the sandbox's 30.2% -- expected and consistent with this project's established rounding-on-unrounded-intermediates convention (see e.g. draugur/kikimora rangeOptimalM notes elsewhere in this file): the sandbox computes missileAppliedFraction() off the UNROUNDED internal sig/speed values, not the already-rounded 79/3790 shown in the UI. Rocket stays #1 in both states here (small/fast ammo vs. a small Interceptor hull in both states), unlike a case where boosting speed enough could flip the ranking to a slower-but-tighter-explosion-radius class -- that flip case is NOT separately covered by a golden fit this session (noted as a disclosed gap, not a silent omission). expected.note: Missile applied-DPS metric correction (2026-10-12, Erik's own design fix). Bare Megathron: sig radius S=380 (hull attr552, live-ESI, unchanged by this fix), cruising speed Vt=152.5 (hull attr37=122 x this file's MAX_NAVIGATION_MULT=1.25-at-V convention). Hand-derived (eveuniversity.org formula, same as the T1-only pass) across all 14 class x tier combinations: under the OLD application%-only ranking, HAM (T1, 100%) and Rocket (Rage, 100%) tie for #1 -- an uninformative tie that tells a pilot nothing about which actually deals more damage. Under the NEW appliedDps ranking (per-shot damage / launcher cycle time x applicationFraction), Cruise Missile Precision wins outright at 17.37 applied DPS despite only 76.6% application -- its much higher per-shot damage (375, vs. HAM's 100 or Rocket Rage's 51.3) more than compensates for not being the single highest-applying choice. Hand-derived value matched the sandboxed estimateHpAndDps() output exactly. This is the concrete 'before vs. after' case demonstrating why the metric correction matters, not just a restatement of the Rifter/Crow fits where the top pick happens to be unchanged either way. Revert-sanity-checked: setting MISSILE_REC_METRIC back to 'applicationPct' in a throwaway copy correctly flips this fit's #1 pick away from Cruise Missile Precision (to a 100%-tied entry, order then decided by object insertion order rather than any real ranking) -- confirms this assertion actually exercises the metric switch, not just coincidence.

expected.note: Hand-verified against Power Diagnostic System II's real dogma attributes (attr144=0.915, attr147=1.05, confirmed via the local pyfa SDE cache): capacity = (250+0)*1.25*1.05 = 328.125 -> 328; rechargeTimeSec = 125000*0.75*0.915/1000 = 85.78125s; peakRechargeRate = 2.5*328.125/85.78125 = 9.56 -> 9.6. Both capacity and peak recharge rate increase vs. the bare-hull baseline (312.5 GJ / 8.3 GJ/s, see rifter_constructed_cap_recharger_group_gate), confirming the KNOWN OPEN ITEM #1 fix's new capCapacityBonusFractions pool is being applied, not just present but inert. 2026-10-12 EXTENDED: also carries attr134=0.915/attr146=1.05 (the matching shield-side recharge/capacity dual-buff, same direction as its already-modeled capacitor-side attr144/147) -- see SHIELD_RECHARGE_RATE_MULT_ATTR/SHIELD_CAPACITY_MULT_ATTR's comments in index.html. rawShieldHP = 562.5*1.05 = 590.625 -> round 591 (up from baseline's 563); shieldRechargeTimeSec = 468.75*0.915 = 428.90625s -> peak = 2.5*590.625/428.90625 = 3.44 -> round 3 (down slightly from baseline's 3.0->3 despite both pools moving in the 'better' direction individually -- the recharge-time cut here, 0.915, is much smaller than Shield Recharger's 0.85 or Flux Coil's 0.7, so the extra capacity it also has to push through ends up a wash at this precision; still a real, correctly-modeled dual-buff with no downside, matching its capacitor-side twin exactly).

Universal always-trained skill stages only: shieldHP_eff = 450*1.25(Shield Management) = 562.5 -> round 563 (rawShieldHP). shieldRechargeTimeSec = 625*0.75(Shield Operation) = 468.75s. peak = 2.5*562.5/468.75 = 3.0 exactly -- clean round number, a strong internal-consistency check that MAX_SHIELD_MGMT_MULT/MAX_SHIELD_OPERATION_MULT are both applying as independent multiplicative stages with no module in the mix at all. shieldBreakPointDps == shieldPassiveRegenDps here since hasShieldRepFlag=0 (no Shield Booster, nothing to add).

209.description: The Scourge heavy missile is an old relic from the Caldari-Gallente War that is still in widespread use because of its low price and versatility.
209.name: Scourge Heavy Missile

210.description: From its humble beginnings in tiny Minmatar design labs, the Scourge light missile has quickly established itself throughout the star cluster as a premier missile for light launchers.
210.name: Scourge Light Missile

266.description: A small rocket with a piercing warhead.
266.name: Scourge Rocket

267.description: An ultra-heavy piercing missile. While it is a slow projectile, its sheer damage potential is simply staggering.
267.name: Scourge Torpedo

2404.description: Favored by many for its average capacity and firing rate. Useful in both fast attack raids and longer battles.
2404.name: Light Missile Launcher II

2410.description: Designed for long engagements between medium sized ships. Slow firing rate, but makes up for it with a large missile capacity.
2410.name: Heavy Missile Launcher II

2420.description: A massive launcher designed for extended bombardments of hard targets like battleships and stations. Contains a huge missile capacity, but has a slow firing rate and trouble targeting small, fast ships.
2420.name: Torpedo Launcher II

2629.description:
The Scourge heavy missile is an old relic from the Caldari-Gallente War that is still in widespread use because of its low price and versatility.

A modified version of the Scourge heavy missile. Does more damage than its predecessor but the volatile nature of the warhead, and its powerful containment system, reduce both flight time and precision.
2629.name: Scourge Fury Heavy Missile

10631.description: A tiny launcher that can carry a very limited supply of rockets. Not really intended as a primary weapon but rather as a cheap supplementary weapon system.
10631.name: Rocket Launcher II

19739.description: A battleship mounted launcher used for long range standoffs with other battleships, but less suitable for bombardment of deployed structures. Contains a huge missile capacity, but has a slow firing rate and trouble targeting small, fast ships.
19739.name: Cruise Missile Launcher II

20307.description: A kinetic warhead designed for use with heavy assault launchers. Heavy assault missiles can be fired at a greater rate than heavy missiles, at the expense of effective range.
20307.name: Scourge Heavy Assault Missile

24471.description:
A small rocket with a piercing warhead.

This modified version of the Scourge rocket packs a considerably stronger punch, but as a result is heavier and slower. This makes it very effective against larger targets, but markedly less effective against smaller and more agile targets.
24471.name: Scourge Rage Rocket

24477.description:
A small rocket with a piercing warhead.

A modified version of the Scourge rocket. It can reach higher velocity than the Scourge rocket at the expense of warhead size.
24477.name: Scourge Javelin Rocket

24495.description:
From its humble beginnings in tiny Minmatar design labs, the Scourge light missile has quickly established itself throughout the star cluster as a premier missile for light launchers.

A modified version of the Scourge light missile. Does more damage than its predecessor but the volatile nature of the warhead, and its powerful containment system, reduce both flight time and precision.
24495.name: Scourge Fury Light Missile

24501.description:
From its humble beginnings in tiny Minmatar design labs, the Scourge light missile has quickly established itself throughout the star cluster as a premier missile for light launchers.

A modified version of the Scourge light missile. Great for taking down smaller ships, but fuel use by stabilization thrusters reduces maximum flight time.
24501.name: Scourge Precision Light Missile

24513.description:

A modified version of the Scourge heavy missile. Great for taking down smaller ships, but fuel use by stabilization thrusters reduces maximum flight time.
24513.name: Scourge Precision Heavy Missile

A modified version of the Scourge cruise. Does more damage than its predecessor but the volatile nature of the warhead, and its powerful containment system, reduce both flight time and precision.
24533.name: Scourge Fury Cruise Missile

24541.description:

25715.description: A launcher intended for use on cruiser-class spacecraft. While assault launchers do not possess the sheer damage-dealing capability of regular heavy missile launchers, their blend of speed and attack power lends them application across a good range of tactical situations.
25715.name: Heavy Assault Missile Launcher II

expected.note: Bare Rifter + 1x Shield Recharger II (real attr134=0.85, confirmed via the local pyfa SDE cache -- no attr146, capacity untouched, confirming it as the 'recharge-only' member of this group unlike Flux Coil/PDS). rawShieldHP unchanged from baseline (563, see rifter_constructed_passive_shield_regen_baseline). shieldRechargeTimeSec = 468.75*0.85 = 398.4375s (single module, no stacking penalty to apply). peak = 2.5*562.5/398.4375 = 3.53 -> round 4, up from the baseline's 3 -- confirms the new shieldRechargeTimePctFractions pool is live.

rifter_constructed_shield_flux_coil.label: CONSTRUCTED (disclosed, see expected.note): bare Rifter + 1x Shield Flux Coil II in a Low slot -- isolates the passive shield recharge fix's attr134+attr146 pair via Shield Flux Coil specifically (trades capacity for recharge speed, same shape as its capacitor-side twin already modeled).

expected.note: Bare Rifter + 1x Shield Flux Coil II (real attr134=0.7 + attr146=0.85, confirmed via the local pyfa SDE cache -- same capacity-for-recharge tradeoff shape as its already-modeled capacitor-side twin). rawShieldHP = 562.5*0.85 = 478.125 -> round 478 (down from baseline's 563, the real tradeoff). shieldRechargeTimeSec = 468.75*0.7 = 328.125s. peak = 2.5*478.125/328.125 = 3.64 -> round 4 -- still up from baseline despite the capacity cut, confirming both shieldRechargeTimePctFractions AND shieldCapacityPctFractions are live and correctly multiplied together rather than one clobbering the other.
